Lauren — quick pass below. I ran the samples through our local perf bench for two model variants: Llama2-13B q8 (baseline) and a quantized q4 variant we onboarded (approx -30% perf impact on latency but 2x throughput on same GPU). Numbers assume batching tuned for sub-200ms GPU processing per batch and network+overhead ~70ms.

Summary (numbers are conservative, include 20% safety):
- Sustained target: 850 TPS (tokens/sec) -> tokens/sec to tokens/gpu/sec mapping depends on tokens per request. From trace median tokens/request = 24 tokens -> 850 TPS maps to ~20 requests/sec (rps) or ~480 tokens/sec request-level? Wait — keep units consistent: we use tokens/sec as primary.

Assumptions: median tokens per generation = 24, avg per-request concurrency = 1.1.

Per-GPU baseline throughput (H100 80GB, fp16 runtime, optimized kernels):
- Llama2-13B fp16: ~300 tokens/sec/GPU (steady with batching)
- Llama2-13B q4 (int8-ish): ~550 tokens/sec/GPU (higher throughput, slightly higher variance)

Peak burst handling (short spikes):
- If we expect 4500 TPS spikes, with q4 GPUs you'd need ~9 GPUs to absorb raw token throughput (4500 / 550 ≈ 8.2). With fp16 you'd need ~15 GPUs.

Recommended configurations:
Option A — Cost-optimized (quantized variant):
- Baseline commit to cover sustained 850 TPS: 2 H100 80GB nodes (assuming 1 GPU per node for simplicity) gives ~1100 tokens/sec capacity -> 1.3x above sustained.
- Burst buffer: elastic burst pool of 8 GPUs for short spikes (on-demand/reserved burst) -> covers 4500 TPS spikes.
- Headroom policy: auto-scale burst up to 9 GPUs for <=5 minutes, auto-fall to baseline after cool-down.

Option B — Latency-optimized (fp16 baseline):
- Baseline commit: 3 H100 GPUs (~900 tokens/sec conservative) plus 12 GPUs for burst (covers 4500 TPS). Lower quantization risk for hallucinations.

Operational notes:
- Warm KV/prefix cache reduces per-request tokens and effective load by ~18–25% for repeat prompts (we observed xfer benefit in traces). If Spectralor can warm the cache for catalog prompts, baseline GPU needs drop by ~1 GPU in Option A.
- Cold-starts: cold KV cache adds an initial penalty of ~120–180ms; factoring that, p95 with Option A (q4) is projected at ~320–380ms depending on batch packing and network variability. Option B keeps p95 < 350ms more consistently.

Runbook excerpt (short):
- Canary: start 72-hour canary at 60% of committed baseline with synthetic traffic matching 95th percentile; verify p95 and token success rate.
- Fallback: On sustained overload >3m, route 10–25% traffic to smaller 6B variant and prioritize critical routes.
- Cache warmup: pre-warm KV for top 500 intents 30m before marketing pushes.

Next steps: I can convert these into a simple capacity table (tokens/sec -> GPUs -> estimated p95) for the commercial blurb. Ben
